description: Requires a TechFabric engineer's Microsoft sign-in (scope blog.write). The site's rule-based checks (slop, claims, known errors, voice, opening, title, description, FAQ, diagram, images, links, a case study's rules) on a post's Markdown, frontmatter included: about a second, free, filing nothing. Iterate with this, never with check_draft: rewrite each passage in rewrite_plan as its fix says and lint again until ready, then review the draft against the judge_rubric it returns. With id, it lints a draft of yours: its saved text, or the markdown you send as an edit to it.

id.description: A draft of yours (the id submit_draft returned). Alone: lints its saved text. With markdown: lints that edit as this draft (its kind, slug, images and sources) before you save it

images.description: The images the post refers to by name (names only; no data needed)

alt.description: What the image shows, for its alt text and caption

data.description: The image's bytes, base64 (PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, at most 10 MB). Required by submit_draft; check_draft needs only the name.

name.description: The file name the post refers to the image by, e.g. pipeline.png

kind.description: What the draft is: "post" (the default, a blog post) or "case-study" (content/case-studies, at /case-studies/<slug>). A case study's frontmatter is title, description, sector, stack, track (ai, migration or other) and client when the client register approves naming them or the engineer says the client agreed (client_confirmed); its body opens with ## Challenge, ## Strategy, ## Solution and ## Results, each with a bold one-line statement first. See the editorial_rules resource.

markdown.description: The whole post: frontmatter (title, description at least) and body

rubric.description: Also return judge_rubric while checks still fail (it comes anyway once they pass)

slug.description: The draft's slug, when it has one already (get_status draft.slug); otherwise it comes from the title

sources.description: The engineer's own words the draft's claims come from, as text. For a post: what the engineer told you about their own work (what they built, measured, saw and decided, and any result, client or number they gave you), quoted as they said it, and their notes; the fact-check treats these as the author's own account of the work, so a first-hand sentence they don't back is a finding. Never write them yourself: ask the engineer. For a case study: the engineer's own notes and the project's records (README, changelog, metrics they gave you) its numbers come from. Every number in the case study is checked against these; one that isn't here is a finding. A source is not an approval: a client's metric also needs the client register's approval. Ask the engineer for outcome numbers; never invent them. At most 100,000 characters.

name: lint_draft

edit_instruction.description: How to show the redlines (edit mode)

judge_rubric.description: What the model-read checks will ask of this draft: sent once the rule-based checks pass, or with rubric: true

mode.description: The writing partner's edit mode (editorial/voices-of-techfabric.md): show the redlines, change only what the engineer accepts

next_action.description: The one next step. Do what instruction says; call is the tool and the arguments the server already knows

ready.description: Every rule-based check passes on this text

redline_plan.description: With id: what to propose with propose_edits, card by card (find, the limit), or what the engineer answers (confirm, ask_author)

redlines.description: rewrite_plan as a redline for the engineer: each passage with its rule, reason, suggestion, state and options. The engineer decides; never hand back a rewritten post

todo.description: The findings as the engineer's to-do list (the draft app's cards): each card's where, why in plain words and remedies

voice.description: How every sentence is said (editorial/voices-of-techfabric.md, "Before you write a sentence"): follow it in the outline, the draft and every rewrite.

title: Lint a draft
